A.defense_attempt: Pipeline tasks are often ordered from fast narrow checks to broader checks, so a team might describe a practical execution sequence this way. However the model itself represents distribution across boundaries and does not make that execution order the definition or proof of sufficiency.
A.problem: Turns a distribution model into a required execution order and treats order compliance as evidence of sufficiency.

B.defense_attempt: Matches the supplied theory: broad base of small isolated tests, interaction checks in the middle, selected broad system paths above, with allocation adapted to risks and feedback cost.

C.defense_attempt: Broad user paths can cover many behaviors and may be important for system-level confidence. But making them the base and using them for most logic branches reverses the described model and sacrifices narrow local feedback.
C.problem: Reverses the common pyramid and overstates broad E2E as the main means of branch-level checking.

D.defense_attempt: Reducing genuine duplicate assertions can simplify a suite. But equal source-code coverage does not test the same boundary, dependency behavior, or user path, so unit coverage alone does not make broader checks redundant.
D.problem: Equates code coverage overlap with equivalence of test purpose and boundary.
